newsitem.title: KENYA: Foreigners trade no shares on Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners trade no shares on Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Foreigners made no deals on the foreign board of the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Monday and offloaded Central Bank of Kenya bonds, bourse officials said.

Brokers said investors reacted warily to the government saying on Friday it would have to cut spending and raise revenue to try to cover a shortfall of $215 million this year because of the IMF halting a key aid package.
"It all depends on the government's next move," buyers said.
Brokers said many foreign investors were taking a wait-and-see approach rather than pulling out of Kenyan stocks.
But the NSE 20-share index fell 24.95 points on Monday to close at 3428.22, from 3453.18, the highest fall since July 15.

Turnover for the fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond stayed high at 230.4 million shillings from 250 million shillings on Friday after news broke of the IMF decision to halt the aid package over corruption.
Brokers said half the turnover was from anxious foreign investors offloading bonds after the IMF decision.
Trades were made at 102.60 percent from between 102.1605 and 102.00 percent.
"Foreign investors are worried about the possibility of losing on exchange rate fluctuations but I don't think we're going to see a mass exodus from the bond market," said a broker.
